$description: Design-system spacing scale, renumbered 2026-09-20 (Ben). It was xs·sm·md·lg·xl·xxl, extracted from the web app's most-frequently-used Tailwind values — which is how it came to have no register above 'page-level separation' and no room to grow. Adding a step ran the t-shirt names out of letters (xxxl, xxxxl), and inserting a step between two existing ones would have been impossible to name at all. Numbering survives both. The bottom of the scale keeps its 4px increments because that is what control padding needs; the top doubles because that is what page layout needs, and 1.33:1 between adjacent steps is why nothing on the old scale separated anything.

1.$description: Tightest gaps — icon-to-label, inline micro-spacing. Was xs.

2.$description: Compact control padding, tight stacks. Was sm.

3.$description: Default gap — the most common spacing value in the app. Was md.

4.$description: Card and panel padding; the side margin at phone width. Was lg.

5.$description: Separation inside a section. Was xl.

6.$description: Between groups on a screen. Was xxl.

7.$description: Band separation — between groups on a layout whose hierarchy is carried by space rather than by boxes. Paired with 1 or 2 inside the group, which puts the ratio at 6:1 or 12:1.

8.$description: The page opening — the gap between the top edge and the first element on a screen that presents ONE thing. Does a header bar's job without occupying the screen.
